title: PRAY PSALM 23 LIKE THIS EVERY MORNING AND SEE THE DIFFERENCE
text: should. Do not say anything. Do not move. Just breathe. Something just walked into this room. You felt it, didn't you? That weight, that warmth, that thickness in the atmosphere. That is not goosebumps. That is not emotion. That is the manifest presence of the shepherd and he came in ahead of me. He knew you were going to be here. He arrived before you did. He was already seated in this moment waiting for you to catch up. And before I say another word, I need you to do something. Look at your phone. Look at your contacts. Look at the names. There is someone right now who is walking through the valley. Not a valley they chose. A valley that chose them. A valley of sickness, of grief, of financial collapse, of confusion so thick they cannot see tomorrow. And the shepherd has positioned you, this word. Not tomorrow. Not when you finish listening. Now. Sharing this is not posting content. Sharing this is rescue. Sharing this is you extending the rod of the shepherd into a valley where someone is lost. Do it as an act of obedience. Do it as an act of love. And then come back because the shepherd has something to say to you personally today. Now, open your Bible to Psalm 23. All six verses. Most people know this Psalm. Very few people have met it. Most people can recite it. Very few people have been transformed by it. Most people quote it at funerals, which is tragic because this Psalm was not written for the dead. It was written for the living. It was written for the mornings. It was written to be prayed, not read. Prayed, decreed, declared, activated. Let me read it to you not as poetry, as prophecy. The Lord is my shepherd, I shall not want. He maketh me to lie down in green pastures. He leadeth me beside the still waters. He restoreth my soul. He leadeth me in the paths of righteousness for his name's sake. Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for thou art with me; thy rod and thy staff they comfort me. Thou preparest a table before me in the presence of mine enemies. Thou anointest my head with oil; my cup runneth over. Surely goodness and mercy shall follow me all the days of my life: and I will dwell in the house of the Lord for ever. Six verses. 118 words in the original King James. And inside those 118 words is the complete blueprint for a transformed life. Inside those words is healing, provision, direction, protection, restoration, favor. Inside those words is everything you have been searching for in 500 other places. David did not write this Psalm from a palace. David wrote this Psalm from experience. He had been the shepherd before he became the king. He knew what a shepherd does when the sheep is lost. He knew what a shepherd does when the sheep is wounded. He knew what a shepherd does in the night season when predators circle. And from that experience, from the hills of Bethlehem, from the sleepless nights under open sky, he wrote this declaration. He wrote it as testimony first, and then as prophecy. There are dimensions to this Psalm that the average believer has never accessed. They read it as comfort. The spirit of God wants you to read it as commission. He wants you to read it as a legal document, a covenant contract signed in the blood of Jesus. Verse one. The Lord is my shepherd. Listen carefully. David did not say the Lord is a shepherd. He did not say the Lord is the shepherd. He said the Lord is my shepherd. My, that is a possessive pronoun loaded with covenant weight. It means he's not available to everyone in the same way he's available to me. It means this relationship is personal, not general. It means I have access to him that is unique to the nature of this covenant. John chapter 10 verse 14, Jesus said, "I am the good shepherd and know my sheep and am known of mine." He knows you, not knows of you, not knows about you, knows you. The original word is ginosko, an intimate experiential knowledge. He knows the weight you carried to bed last night. He knows the prayer you prayed in your car where no one could hear you. He knows the name you write in your journal that you have not spoken out loud in months. He knows you and he has chosen to be your shepherd. So, the first thing you declare every morning is this, declare it now, declare it out loud. The Lord is my shepherd, not was, not will be, I S, present tense, active tense, today tense. He's shepherding me right now. He's guiding my steps right now. He is watching my path right now. And the moment you establish that the rest follows. I shall not want. Not I hope I will not be in need. Not I am believing that my needs will be met. shall not want. It is a prophetic declaration of total sufficiency. Philippians 4:19, "But my God shall supply all your need according to his riches in glory by Christ Jesus." All your need, every category, every dimension, financial need covered, emotional need covered, physical need covered, relational need covered, spiritual need covered. Your shepherd does not have a partial supply. He has riches in glory. I decree and declare over every life under the sound of this voice, you shall not want. Not this week, not this month, not this year. The shepherd has guaranteed your supply. By the power of the blood of Jesus, receive it. Verse two. He maketh me to lie down in green pastures. He leadeth me beside the still waters. He maketh, not he suggests, not he recommends, maketh. There is a holy insistence in your shepherd. He will not watch you run yourself into the ground. He will not watch you exhaust your anointing chasing things you already prepared for you to simply walk into. He will compel you toward rest when you are too stubborn to choose it for yourself. Matthew chapter 11 verse 28. Jesus said, "Come on to me, all ye that labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest." He's not asking you to come when you are better. He's not asking you to come when you have sorted yourself out. He says, "Come in your labor. Come in your heaviness. Come as you are, and I will give you rest." Green pastures, not dry pastures, not barren pastures. Um, green. Everywhere your shepherd takes you, it is abundant. It is flourishing. It is nourishing. It is more than enough. Still waters. Sheep cannot drink from turbulent water. They will refuse it. The shepherd knows this, so he leads them to still water. He creates peace in the environment before he brings the sheep to drink. This is what he does for you every morning. Before you walk into your day, he prepares the atmosphere. He goes ahead and stills the waters. He goes ahead and clears the turbulence. And then he says, "Come. It is safe. Drink." Hear me, this is not theology. This is encounter. When you pray this verse every morning, you are not reciting poetry. You are activating a divine promise. You are releasing the shepherd into your day ahead of you. You are saying, "Go before me. Prepare my path. Still my waters. Lay my table." Thus saith the spirit of God. The anxiety that wakes up with you every morning is a liar. The fear that makes your heart race before your feet touch the floor is a liar. The shepherd has already moved in that direction. He has already secured the path. You are walking into a future that your shepherd has already visited. Verse 3, "He restoreth my soul. He leadeth me in the paths of righteousness for his name's sake." He restoreth my soul. This is the verse that should make every broken person weep. Not weep in sorrow, weep in relief. Because the word restore in the Hebrew is shub. It means to bring back, to return, to cause to go again. It means to take something that was lost, stolen, or damaged and return it to its original condition. He restores your soul. Not just your circumstances, your soul. The seat of your will, the seat of your emotions, the seat of your desires. The part of you that the world has been trying to wear down since the day you were born. The part of you that got damaged in that relationship. The part of you that was bruised in that betrayal. The part of you that went silent after that loss. He restores it. He reaches into the broken places and he brings them back. Joel 2:25, "And I will restore to you the years that the locusts have eaten." Not approximate. Not mostly. Restore. Full measure. Pressed down. Shaken together. Running over. Someone under the sound of my voice right now, your soul has been in a state of drought for a long time. You'll go through the motions, you show up, you smile when you are expected to smile, but something on the inside has been running on empty. Something on the inside dried up and you cannot remember exactly when it happened. The Lord says, "I see the drought. I am the rain. I decree restoration of soul right now by the power of the Holy Ghost." Let the waters of the spirit flood every dry place in you. Let the joy of the Lord, which is your strength, Nehemiah 8:10, return to your soul this morning. Paths of righteousness for his name's sake. Not for your performance, not because you earned it, for his name's sake. This means your keeping is tied to the reputation of God. It means when God guides you and protects you and provides for you, he is doing it partly to demonstrate who he is to a watching world. You are a testimony in motion. You are a living advertisement for the faithfulness of God. And God does not advertise with broken products. He will make sure you arrive at your destination because his name is on the package. I need you to stay with me. We are only halfway through six verses and already the atmosphere has changed. I need you to feel what David felt when he wrote this. He was not writing from theory, he was writing from the hill. He was writing from the sleepless night with the lion. He was writing from the moment the bear came and God held the bear. He was writing from the valley and he had made it through. Verse 4, "Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for thou art with me. Thy rod and thy staff, they comfort me. Though I walk through not if I ever face a valley, not in the unlikely event of a dark season, though I walk through. David is acknowledging the valley. He's not pretending the valley does not exist. He's not preaching a gospel that says the redeemed never face darkness. He's saying, "Yes, the valley is real. Yes, the shadow is real. But here is what is more real, thou art with me." The shepherd does not uh lift you above the valley. He walks through the valley with you. That is the nature of this shepherd. He does not send a proxy. He does not send a representative. He comes personally. Isaiah chapter 43, verse two. "When thou passest through the waters, I will be with thee. And through the rivers, they shall not overflow thee. When thou walkest through the fire, thou shalt not be burned. Neither shall the flame kindle upon thee." When you pass through waters, not if. He's not promising you a life without fire. He's promising you fire that does not consume you. He's promising you water that does not drown you. He's promising you a valley that does not define you. The shadow of death. A shadow has no substance. A shadow has no power. A shadow can only exist if there is a light source. And if there is a shadow, there is also a light. The very shadow that threatens you is proof that the light is present. You cannot have a shadow without a source. And the light of the world, John 8:12, is your shepherd. "I will fear no evil." This is not passive. This is a declaration of war. This is you looking fear in the face with the rod of the shepherd in your hand and saying, "Not today. You have no authority here. My shepherd walks with me and he carries a rod. And that rod has broken the back of lions that were bigger than you. The rod is discipline. The rod is correction. The rod is warfare. The staff is comfort. The staff is guidance. The staff is intimacy. The shepherd has both. He is not a soft shepherd with sentimental words and no power. He is the shepherd who fights for his sheep. Every altar erected against your peace, I pull it down by fire. Every spirit of fear that has been assigned to torment your night, I bind it by the blood of Jesus. Every shadow that has been following you through your valley, I command the light of God to dissolve it. You are walking through, not dwelling in, through. The valley has an exit and your shepherd knows exactly where it is. Verse five. Thou preparest a table before me in the presence of mine enemies. Thou anointest my head with oil. My cup runneth over. Stop right there. Did you read what I just read? God does not remove the enemies before he sets the table. He sets the table in the presence of the enemies. This is one of the most radical verses in all of scripture because it means your feast happens where the fight is. It means your promotion happens in front of the people who tried to stop you. It means your blessing is publicly served in the very arena where the attack was launched. The spirit of God is saying something right now. He is saying, I did not promise you that your enemies would disappear. I promised you that they would watch. They would sit in the front row of your vindication. They would watch with their own eyes as I honor you in the room where they tried to shame you. They would watch as I promote you in the department where they tried to demote you. They would watch as I give you the contract they thought they had already taken from you. Psalm 37:34. Wait on the Lord and keep his way and he shall exalt thee to inherit the land. When the wicked are cut off, thou shalt see it. You shall see it. You will be present for the reversal. You will not miss the vindication. You will sit at the table that the shepherd prepared, and your enemies will serve as your witnesses. Thou anointest my head with oil. Anointing in scripture is not just about ministry. Anointing is consecration. It means set apart, marked, chosen, protected. When the shepherd anoints your head, he's marking you as his. He's saying, "This one belongs to me. Touch not my anointed. Do my prophet no harm." First Chronicles 16:22, "My cup runneth over." Not my cup is full. Not my cup is sufficient. Runneth over. The shepherd does not give you enough. He gives you overflow. He does not give you what you need. He gives you more than you need. So much more that there is enough for you and enough for everyone around you. This is the economy of the kingdom. Luke 6:38, "Give, and it shall be given unto you. Good measure, pressed down, and shaken together, and running over." I decree and declare your cup is running over. Every area of lack in your life, it is being addressed by the overflow economy of heaven. Every financial drought, the cup is being filled, and it will overflow. Every relational emptiness, the cup is being filled. Every spiritual dryness, the oil of the Holy Ghost is being poured without measure. There is a man, I see him clearly. His name begins with D. He has been operating at a deficit for 18 months. Every month he has done the mathematics, and the mathematics does not work. He has been too ashamed to tell anyone the full picture. The Lord says to that man, "I have been counting every month you trusted me in the deficit. I have been recording every tithe you paid when you did not have enough to pay it. I have been watching every act of faithfulness in the season of scarcity. And the Lord says the season of scarcity is ending with this week. Your cup is about to run over. And when it does, you will not be able to contain it. Verse 6, "Surely goodness and mercy shall follow me all the days of my life, and I will dwell in the house of the Lord forever." Surely. Not perhaps, not probably, not under the right conditions. Surely. This is the language of absolute certainty. This is covenant language. This is blood language. This is the shepherd putting his reputation on the line and saying, "I guarantee this." Goodness and mercy. Two divine escort agents assigned to your life. They are not in front of you, they are following you. Wherever you go, goodness is tracking you. Whatever room you walk into, mercy is right behind you cleaning up what needs to be cleaned. Mercy for your past, goodness for your future. Mercy that covers what you got wrong. Goodness that secures what you cannot secure yourself. You are not walking through life unaccompanied. You are flanked, you are escorted, you are covered. All the days of my life. Not the good days only, all days. The Monday that feels like a Monday, the season that feels impossible. The year that almost broke you. All the days. There is not a single day on your calendar that goodness and mercy are on leave. They are on assignment every single morning that you wake up. And then he ends with the most powerful declaration of all. "I will dwell in the house of the Lord forever." This is not wishful thinking. This is a covenant vow. This is the sheep saying, "I am not going anywhere. My address is my shepherd's house." I am planted. I am rooted. I am established. Psalm 92:13, "Those that be planted in the house of the Lord shall flourish in the courts of our God." Flourish. That is your word. That is your declaration for every morning. Now, this is where we shift. This is where the teaching becomes activation. This is where the revelation becomes fire. I want you to stand. I want you to lift your hands. And I want you to pray Psalm 23 not as a reader, as a son, as a daughter. Pray it like you own it because you do. Pray it like you wrote it because the blood of Jesus has given you legal title to every word. Father God, we come before you on the foundation of your word. We come before you through the blood of Jesus. Hebrews 10:19, with boldness to enter the holiest. Not because we are worthy, because he was. Not because we have been perfect, because the blood has covered our imperfection. And Father, we stand on this blood today and we declare Psalm 23 over our lives. We declare the Lord is our shepherd. You are my shepherd, not a shepherd I have heard about, not a shepherd someone else knows. My shepherd, personally assigned to me. You know my name. You know my voice. You know my fears. You know the dreams I carry that I have never spoken to a human being and you are shepherding me right now this morning. Because you are my shepherd, I shall not want. I declare war on the spirit of lack. I declare war on the poverty mindset that has been assigned to my thinking. I declare war on every spirit of scarcity that has tried to convince me that there is not enough. My God shall supply all my need. Philippians 4:19, according to his riches in glory, not according to the economy, not according to the exchange rate, not according to my salary, according to his riches in glory. And his riches are inexhaustible. I decree every financial gate that has been closed over my life, open in the name of Jesus. Every embargo on my income lifted by the blood of the lamb. Every witchcraft altar that has been consuming my resources before they reach me, destroyed by fire. Every spirit of poverty that has followed my bloodline, you are evicted today. I shall not want. I decree it. I establish it. I enforce it. Father, he maketh me to lie down in green pastures. I receive the rest of the shepherd. I break the spirit of striving that has been driving me into exhaustion. I break the yoke of anxiety that has stolen my sleep, my peace, my stillness. Matthew 11:28, I come to you, Lord. I come with my labor. I come with my heaviness, and I receive right now the rest that only a shepherd can give. He leads me beside still waters. I speak peace over my mind, peace that passeth all understanding. Philippians 4:2-7, I speak peace over my household. Every storm that has been raging in my home, be still. The same voice that spoke to the wind and the waves in Mark 4:39, that voice speaks over my situation today, peace, be still. Every covenant your ancestors entered that is still haunting your peace, it is annulled tonight by the blood of Jesus. Every generational spirit of turmoil, it is broken. Every familiar spirit that has been assigned to create confusion in your life, I bind it. Silence by fire, now. Receive my soul. Father, restore. Restore everything that was taken. Restore the joy that grief stole. Restore the faith that disappointment eroded. Restore the confidence that abuse and rejection dismantled. Restore the fire that religion without encounter extinguished. Restore the dreams that delay tried to bury. I speak to every soul under the sound of this voice. The drought is ending. The shepherd is walking into the dry places of your life right now with water. Isaiah 43:19, "Behold, I will do a new thing. Now it shall spring forth. Shall you not know it? I will even make a way in the wilderness and rivers in the desert." Rivers in your desert. Right now, there is a young woman, I see her, she walked away from the faith 3 years ago. Something happened, a disappointment so deep it shook everything she believed. She has not prayed properly since. She has been watching from a distance, wondering if God still wants her. The shepherd says, "I left the 99 to find you." Luke 15:4, "I have been in the wilderness looking for you every single day. Come home. The table is still set. Your seat is still waiting." I decree restoration. Full restoration of faith. Full restoration of fire. He leadeth me in the paths of righteousness for his name's sake. Father, lead us. Every decision that is pending, lead. Every door that is open, lead. Every door that looks open but is actually a trap, close it. Proverbs 3:5-6, "Trust in the Lord with all your heart. Lean not to your own understanding. In all your ways, acknowledge him and he shall direct your paths." I decree divine direction over every major decision this week. The right doors will be obvious, the wrong doors will be exposed. No detours, no dead ends, no costly wrong turns. The shepherd leads and because he leads, you arrive. I speak to marriages under the sound of this voice. Every home that the enemy has been trying to dismantle, I release the peace of the shepherd into that home. I decree communication restored, trust rebuilt, intimacy renewed. Every third party operating as a weapon against covenant marriages be exposed and removed. What God joined together, Matthew 19:2-6, let no man, no devil, no destruction separate. I speak to the singles who are believing for covenant marriage. The shepherd is leading you to still waters, not turbulent connections, not someone who will disturb your peace, not someone who will derail your destiny. The right person is being positioned, the paths are being aligned. Wait on the shepherd. He does not give the sheep bad pasture. Yeah, though I walk through the valley, Father, we acknowledge the valleys. Some of us are in the valley right now, not approaching the valley in IT. The shadow is real, the darkness is real, the pressure is real, but we decree thou art with me. We are not in this valley alone. The shepherd came into the valley with us and he's already mapping our exit. I speak to everyone who has been diagnosed with a terminal report. I speak to everyone who received news in the last 90 days that shook the foundation of their world. The shepherd walks in the valley of the shadow of death and the shadow does not touch him and because you are with him, the shadow does not get to touch you either. By the blood of Jesus, I speak healing. Every cancer cell, death to it in the name of Jesus, every organ under attack, I speak divine repair, supernatural reconstruction. Everybody fighting disease right now, the rod of the shepherd strikes that disease. Isaiah 53:2-5, by his stripes we are healed. Not we will be healed, we are healed. Receive it, enforce it, walk in it. I speak to mental health. Every spirit of depression that has been sitting on a mind under this voice, I command it to lift now. The spirit of God is not a spirit of fear, 2 Timothy 1:2-7, but of power and of love and of a sound mind. Sound mind, not a shattered mind, not a tormented mind, sound. I decree soundness of mind over every person engaging with this prayer. There is a woman, her name is Esther. She has been in a valley of grief for 7 months. She lost someone and the loss has hollowed her out. She has been functioning on the outside and collapsing on the inside. The shepherd says to Esther, "I am in this valley with you. I have been collecting your tears, Psalm 56:2-8. Every tear is in my bottle, none has been wasted. And I am about to turn your mourning into dancing, Psalm 32:11. Not next year, this season. Watch me. Thou preparest a table before me in the presence of mine enemies. Father, set the table, set it publicly, set it visibly, set it in the very arena where the enemy thought he had won. I speak to the person who was overlooked for the promotion. I speak to the business that was undercut by a competitor. I speak to the ministry that was criticized and mocked in its early stages. I speak to the dream that was publicly dismissed by people who should have supported it. The table is being prepared and your enemies have reserved seats. They will watch, they will witness, they will be unable to deny what God has done. Every altar erected against your lifting, I pull it down by fire. Every witchcraft coven that has deliberated against your promotion, their verdict is overturned. Every evil tongue that spoke against your destiny, Isaiah 54:17, it is condemned. Thou anointest my head with oil. Father, anoint fresh oil, new oil, oil that breaks every yoke, Isaiah 10:27. I receive the anointing of the Holy Ghost over my life this morning, over my ministry, over my business, over my family, over my calling. Let the anointing distinguish me. Let it make room for me, Proverbs 18:16. Let it attract the right people, let it repel the wrong ones. Let it open doors that no amount of human effort could have opened. My cup runneth over. I receive overflow, overflow in my finances, overflow in my health, overflow in my relationships, overflow in my anointing, overflow in my creativity, overflow in my joy. More than enough so that I become a resource for the people around me. Blessed to be a blessing, Genesis 12:2. I decree unexpected income arrives this week. I decree unexplained favor opens doors that have been shut for years. I decree divine connections are activated, people who carry keys to your next level are being aligned. The angels are moving, Hebrews 1:14. Ministering spirits dispatched for the heirs of salvation. They have assignments, I release them now. Go, prepare the table, activate the favor, position the breakthrough. Surely surely goodness and mercy shall follow me. I declare this over every morning of my life from this morning forward. Goodness go before me today. Make the rough places plain. Mercy cover everything behind me. Cover the mistakes. Cover the gaps. Cover the insufficiency. I am flanked by the covenantal escorts of heaven. Nothing comes at me that does not first pass through goodness and mercy. All the days of my life, this day, this week, this year, every day that remains in this life, it is covered by the shepherding of the Lord. I speak divine preservation over every life connected to this prayer. No premature departure. No untimely death. No unexplained accident. Psalm will not slumber. Psalm 91, a thousand shall fall at thy side and 10,000 at thy right hand, but it shall not come nigh thee. The covering is active. The preservation is enforced. The blood is speaking. I will dwell in the house of the Lord forever. I am planted. I am not uprooted. Every attempt to displace me from my covenant position, it fails. Every plan to cut me off from my source, it fails. I am rooted. I am established. I am flourishing. Psalm 92 to 13, planted in the house of the Lord, flourishing in the courts of our God. Father, we thank you. We thank you because this prayer is not just words. This prayer is covenant enforcement. Every word of Psalm 23 is a check signed in the blood of Jesus and we have just presented it at the counter of heaven, and heaven never bounces a check. There is a man, I see the name Peter. He has been running from an assignment. He knows what God has called him to do, but the fear of failure has paralyzed him for 2 years. He has been preparing to prepare. The Lord says to Peter, "The shepherd does not call the equipped. He equips the called. Stop waiting until you feel ready. The rod and the staff are in your hands. Take the next step. I will do the rest." I speak to generational destiny. Every person engaging with this prayer, who is the first in their family to believe, you are not just changing your story, you are rewriting the script for everyone after you. Every child that will come from your lineage, they will be born into a covenant that you established. Every grandchild, every great-grandchild, they will walk into blessings that were unlocked by your faithfulness. I decree generational shift, generational blessing, generational glory. What was broken stops breaking. What was cursed starts flourishing now. The siege is over. Every morning from this morning, you are going to wake up differently. You are going to open your eyes, and before your feet touch the ground, you are going to speak. "The Lord is my shepherd. I shall not want." And heaven is going to respond. The goodness and mercy that were assigned to you from eternity are going to move into position. The table that was prepared for you is going to be set fresh. The anointing on your head is going to be renewed. The cup that was empty is going to overflow again. This is not a one-time prayer. This is a lifestyle. This is the daily rhythm of the son who knows his shepherd. This is how you start every morning from this morning forward. Walk into your favor, it has been waiting. Your blessings know your name and your shepherd has given them your address. Your destiny is preserved by the blood. I decree this week is not ordinary. You prayed Psalm 23 with authority this morning. You commanded the morning. You activated the covenant and something that has been stuck for a long time is about to move. Something that has been closed is about to open. Something that has been silent is about to speak in your favor. From this altar you go as a carrier of the shepherd's presence. Wherever you go today, the table goes with you. Wherever you go, goodness and mercy escort you. Wherever you go, the shepherd walks beside you. Shondai ecclesia tumbalare kaishondai ecclesia tumbalare kaishondai. It is done. The shepherd has spoken. Heaven has witnessed. Hell has been served notice. The Lord is your shepherd. You shall not want. Not today, not tomorrow, not ever. Amen and amen.
